brief: Weekly summary (Mark Wilson, forwarding Dioni Ellinikaki) of Goldman's 2027 outlook suite, set against a week where a record one-day equity selloff fully reversed by midweek, then reversed again on hotter inflation, higher yields and the ousting of the founder-CEO of the world's largest company. GS forecasts 2.8% global GDP growth in 2027 (vs 2.7% in 2026) and slowing inflation, with 2 more Fed hikes and 1 ECB hike (below market pricing) before both banks cut by year-end. Downside risks are Middle East/energy uncertainty and a slowing AI investment boom. Earnings growth decelerates everywhere (US EPS 36% to 11%, Europe 18% to 7%, Japan 24% to 9%), so GS stays Overweight US and Japan, Underweight Europe, and downgrades European banks, even though European banks have beaten the 'Mag7' over 1 to 5 years and the CAC-40 has beaten GS's AI-winner basket over 12 months. AI capex rises from $1.1tn to $1.8tn but the investment impulse peaks in 1H27, already priced in after the Democratic midterm sweep. GIR calls duration attractive (10y UST at 4.6%, current pricing too hawkish) and argues Europe is a resilient AI hedge, supported by falling Brent toward $78/bbl, lower yields, buybacks and shrinking equity supply, favoring Retailers, Utilities, Telecoms and the DAX over Energy, Banks and Insurance.
